description: The hand-verified expected result for the negative Dependency-Check fixture that reaches the unresolvable_path rejection class. No record in the fixture is defective: all six are sound, and the condition is a property of the recorded path base rather than of any record, so the fixture is evaluated under a metadata variant whose path_base.kind is 'none'. The top-level rows, counts, counters and rejections in this file describe that variant; contrast_under_the_recorded_base carries the same fixture's outcome under the base harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json actually records, which is six rows and no rejection. Every value was derived by reading the fixture together with the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/, never by running the adapter and recording what it printed. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/dependency_check.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match. Read rejection_class first -- it derives the class from paths.py and states exactly why the recorded base cannot reach it.
rules: No user-specified rule governs this file. review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided.', which is the complete document; AAP 0.7 and AAP 0.10.2 say the same. Enterprise best practice applies in their place, held to the AAP's own bar: hand-verify rather than record a run, reject rather than infer, and state an absence rather than omit it. This file exists because of AAP 0.6.1, AAP 0.6.2 and AAP 0.9.4, not because of a rule.

fixture.line_ending: LF, with a trailing newline and no CR anywhere
fixture.why_no_record_is_defective: This fixture's subject is the recorded metadata, not the artifact. Every one of its six records is an object with a usable name, a usable description, a usable filePath and a formable package coordinate, and under the base this provisioning actually records all six become rows -- which is what contrast_under_the_recorded_base fixes. A fixture that also carried a defective record would confound the two causes and could not establish which one produced which outcome.
fixture.derived_from: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/reject-dependency-check-unresolvable-path.json (sha256 cef4785fa3afbe45a741d7b08fa4468e697ce1da0fb44562c4a6fa83a9e5cfd8), the sibling negative fixture in this tree, itself derived from the positive oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/dependency-check.json (sha256 53fb2fa91725148f1b33df951f95e8ee01ef98ec62bebb10b73bd541bf10de68)
derivation: seven of the sibling's eight dependencies were carried unchanged: its indices 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 became this fixture's 0 through 6, in that order. Each is byte-identical to the sibling's element under canonical comparison -- isVirtual, fileName, filePath, the hash triple where present, evidenceCollected, packages[], vulnerabilityIds[] and every member of vulnerabilities[].

the sibling's index 2 was EXCLUDED: the ui-test/package-lock.json dependency whose filePath is the empty string, together with both its vulnerabilities. It is left out because an empty filePath is caught by resolve_recorded_path's FIRST branch, absent_path, which precedes the PATH_BASE_KIND_NONE branch this fixture is about. Keeping it would put two rejection classes in a fixture whose whole subject is one, and would make the shared-detail property below untestable.
nothing was added, edited or reordered. No field of any carried element differs from the sibling's, which is why this fixture has no defective record at all.
reportSchema, scanInfo (engineVersion 13.0.0 and all four dataSource timestamps) and projectInfo are byte-identical to the sibling's, and through it to harness/artifacts/raw/dependency-check.json.
fixture.captured_provenance: A negative fixture is derived from the captured one rather than being an excerpt of it, so the provenance is stated per dependency instead of claimed for the file. Envelopes captured verbatim from the raw artifact: indices 0, 1 and 6 (the bootstrap bundle, the jquery.cookies bundle and the ui static package.json). Envelopes authored in the positive sibling and carried through the negative sibling: indices 2 and 3. Envelopes authored in the negative sibling and carried here: indices 4 and 5, the two archive members. Every packages[] and every vulnerabilities[] array in this shape is authored, as the positive sibling's own fixture block records -- the raw artifact carries 32 dependencies with zero vulnerabilities and zero packages, so no excerpt of it can exercise a single field of this adapter's row builder.
fixture.authored_shapes_follow: Dependency-Check 13.0.0's own report members, as verified against the raw artifact and against the field names harness/lib/normalize/adapters/dependency_check.py reads: source, name, severity, unscored, cvssv2.score, cvssv3.baseScore, cvssv4.baseScore, cwes[], description, notes, references[], vulnerableSoftware[], packages[].id and the isVirtual/evidenceCollected pair a virtual dependency carries.
fixture.archive_shape_provenance: The concatenated-member convention the two archive dependencies exercise -- the member joined onto the container with a '/' and no separator of any kind -- is recorded in harness/lib/normalize/adapters/dependency_check.py's module docstring as measured on this provisioning's own tool, quoting the same Guava-POM-inside-spark-network-common coordinate. It is NOT present in harness/artifacts/raw/dependency-check.json: that artifact's 32 dependencies are all vendored web assets, and zero of their filePath values carry a '.jar/' segment. Stated rather than implied, because a reader who assumed these two records were captured would be wrong about where the shape came from.
fixture.member_existence_corroborated: Both archive coordinates name a member that really exists, as the sibling expectation records: each container contains META-INF/maven/com.google.guava/guava/pom.xml, verified by reading the archive directories. That does not change the path kind or the in_scope field -- an archive member is a non-filesystem coordinate either way -- and it matters here only for the contrast block, since under this file's own variant no path is resolved at all.
fixture.no_secret_or_credential_value: Nothing in this fixture is a secret, a credential or a credential-shaped string. Its findings are dependency advisories -- CVE and Sonatype identifiers against package coordinates -- and no field carries a value to redact.
fixture.fixture_is_never_edited_to_suit_these_ro: The direction is one-way: these expectations are derived from the fixture. If the adapter disagrees with this file, the adapter or this file is wrong and the fixture is not touched.
fixture.re_derivation_trigger: These expectations are re-derived when the fixture changes, which is what the recorded sha256 above makes visible.

routing.detected_by: normalize.shape -- not SARIF, since the document carries neither a version of '2.1.0' nor a runs array, and the native detector keys on the reportSchema/scanInfo/dependencies triple this shape carries
routing.routing_is_metadata_independent: Shape detection reads the document and nothing else, so the variant this file is evaluated under cannot change the route. The same artifact routes to the same adapter under both bases, which is what makes the two outcomes comparable.
routing.not_a_shape_failure: No normalize.shape.UnknownArtifactShape is expected here. This document is a well-formed Dependency-Check report and every record in it is sound; the rejection arises from the recorded path base, not from the shape and not from a record.
routing.negative_routing_test: The mandated negative routing assertion -- that a native artifact must not route to the SARIF adapter -- belongs to test_shape_routing_negative.py and is not restated as an expectation of this fixture.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. The rows in contrast_under_the_recorded_base carry all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted. This file's own top-level rows array is empty, so the order is stated rather than exercised there.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent -- which is the structural reason a record with no resolvable path can only be a rejection.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. Under this file's variant no row is emitted, so the allowlist is never consulted; the glob each row matched under the recorded base is recorded per row in the contrast block.

reference_case_for: the unresolvable_path rejection class for this adapter -- the one path-family class the recorded filesystem_absolute base cannot reach from any record's content, reached here by varying the recorded metadata rather than by shaping a document
a rejection whose cause is entirely outside the artifact: six sound records, one shared detail, six distinct identities, and the same six records becoming six rows under the other branch

the reported_path / filePath divergence on an archive record -- the identity carries the raw concatenated value under filePath and the prepared '!'-separated value under reported_path, which is only visible on a rejection because a row discards the intermediate form
the reconciliation identity at its zero-row boundary: six records, zero rows, six rejections, and the identity still has to balance

resolution_context.evaluated_under: a metadata variant, not the recorded metadata
resolution_context.root_dependence: Every filePath in this artifact is filesystem-absolute and carries /opt/spark-src as a literal prefix, so the contrast block's rows are stated for that root. This file's own outcome is root-independent: the PATH_BASE_KIND_NONE branch returns before the root is used for anything, so the six rejections, their details and their identities are the same whatever absolute root the adapter is given. The root is recorded anyway, because the calling test passes one and a reader should be able to see which.

metadata_variant.scenario: The fixture adapted with a ToolPathBase for dependency-check whose kind is paths.PATH_BASE_KIND_NONE and whose base_value is null, with the tool identifier, the record_path_field and the allowlist unchanged. Exactly one input differs from the recorded context, so the difference in outcome is attributable to it.
metadata_variant.record_path_field_note: Carried over from the recorded metadata unchanged. It is not used by the PATH_BASE_KIND_NONE branch -- only the absent_path branch interpolates it into a detail -- and it is kept identical so the variant differs in the kind alone.
metadata_variant.scan_root_in_the_variant_metadata: Whatever the calling test's metadata document records. It is never consulted: ToolPathBase.base_for_relative returns None for this kind, and the branch rejects rather than falling back to the scan root, which is the whole behaviour under test.
metadata_variant.how_the_variant_is_constructed: By writing a minimal runner-metadata document inside the calling test's own temporary directory and loading it through paths.load_runner_metadata and paths.tool_path_base -- the route test_dependency_check_adapter.Environment.base_of_kind already provides. Never by editing harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json: that document is the gate's record of the provisioning as it was found, and editing its path_base to make a class reachable would falsify a record this run is required to preserve (AAP 0.3.2, AAP 0.8.1).
metadata_variant.authority_for_the_instruction: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json's own path_base_kind_vocabulary, whose 'none' entry reads: 'No explicit base could be established from the runner. paths.py must reject such a record under unresolvable_path rather than fall back.' The instruction is the recorded document's, not this file's, and paths.resolve_recorded_path quotes it back in the detail.
metadata_variant.what_is_not_being_asserted: That this provisioning's dependency-check runner has no establishable base. It has one -- kind filesystem_absolute -- and that is recorded below. The variant is a hypothetical provisioning, exercised so the rejection branch the vocabulary mandates is covered by a committed fixture rather than only by prose.

recorded_metadata_for_this_tool.source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, tools.dependency-check.path_base -- read as input, never assumed
recorded_metadata_for_this_tool.evidence: The runner builds one absolute --scan argument per allowlist directory (18 in a single invocation, invocations_per_run 1), so dependencies[].filePath is filesystem-absolute under the scan root and the resolution is a straight relativization.
recorded_metadata_for_this_tool.working_directory: /opt/spark-src -- equal to the scan root, and deliberately NOT the path base: the tool reports absolute paths because it was handed absolute --scan arguments, not because of where the process ran.
recorded_metadata_for_this_tool.why_it_is_recorded_here: So the variant is legible as a variant, and so this file does not read as a claim about the provisioning. Under this metadata all six records become rows, which is what contrast_under_the_recorded_base fixes.

resolution_context.path_basis_note: No basis is recorded on any outcome here, because no path was resolved. A basis describes how a path was arrived at, and the 'none' branch returns before any arrival. The contrast block records absolute-relativized-to-root on four rows and archive-member-serialized on two, which is where a basis belongs.
resolution_context.path_kinds_note: No path kind either, and for the same reason. Every path_kind_* counter is therefore 0, and that 0 means 'no path was produced' rather than 'a path was produced and was of another kind'.
resolution_context.archive_preparation_still_happens: dependency_check.prepare_file_path runs BEFORE the resolver is called, so the two archive records' values are prepared -- the '!' inserted -- even though nothing is resolved. That is why reported_path differs from filePath on rejections 4 and 5 while archive_references_split stays 0: the counter is incremented on the row-emitting path only, so preparation happening is visible in the identities rather than in the counters.
resolution_context.start_line: Not reached. Dependency-Check reports at dependency granularity -- a vulnerable component, not a line of code -- and this artifact carries no line information in any member at any depth, so start_line would be null on every row in any case. It is also why no reject-dependency-check-non-integer-start-line fixture exists: there is no start_line in this shape for a non-integer to occupy.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: Not reached. Step 5 runs after step 4, and step 4 rejects every record here, so no coordinate is taken even though every dependency carries a formable one. For this shape an unformable coordinate is a rejection rather than a null field, and that rejection belongs to reject-dependency-check-no-package-coordinate.json.
resolution_context.count_unit: dependencies[].vulnerabilities[] -- one vulnerability is one record, whatever the dependency around it does

rejection_class.expected_class_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_UNRESOLVABLE_PATH constant -- a literal member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES, spelled 'unresolvable_path' there and quoted rather than paraphrased here.
derivation: each record's filePath is a non-empty string, so resolve_recorded_path's first branch -- value is None or a blank string, which yields REJECT_ABSENT_PATH -- does not fire
each value is a string, so the second branch -- a non-string value, which yields REJECT_MALFORMED_RECORD -- does not fire either
the third branch raises PathPolicyError for PATH_BASE_KIND_BYTECODE_CLASS, which is the Joern adapter's kind and not this one's, so it is not reached

the fourth branch tests the recorded kind against PATH_BASE_KIND_NONE and returns REJECT_UNRESOLVABLE_PATH with the detail quoted in every rejection below. Under the variant this file is evaluated for, that is the branch every record takes
the branches after it -- archive handling, absolute relativization, per-section targets and the relative-against-base join -- are never reached, so no path is produced and no basis is recorded
the adapter's step 4 returns whatever paths.py classified, verbatim and unreworded, which is what makes the class paths.py's decision rather than the adapter's
rejection_class.why_the_recorded_base_cannot_reach_this_: runner-metadata.json records path_base.kind 'filesystem_absolute' for dependency-check, and ToolPathBase.base_for_relative returns the recorded base value for that kind -- only bytecode_class, per_section_target and none return None. So under the recorded metadata every branch that yields REJECT_UNRESOLVABLE_PATH is closed: an absolute filePath relativizes, a relative one resolves against /opt/spark-src, an archive reference with a relative container resolves against the same base, and the kind is not 'none'. The path-family classes reachable from a record's content alone are therefore absent_path (None, empty or whitespace-only) and malformed_record (a non-string filePath, or an archive reference that cannot be serialized).
rejection_class.relationship_to_the_sibling_expectation: expected/reject-dependency-check-unresolvable-path.rows.json establishes exactly that unreachability, branch by branch, in its why_unresolvable_path_is_unreachable_for_this_adapter block, and records that its own fixture -- whose slug also says unresolvable-path -- produces absent_path instead. Both files are correct and they compose rather than conflict: the class is unreachable from any RECORD's content under the recorded base, and it is reachable from the METADATA, which is the input this file varies. The sibling's what_would_have_to_change_for_unresolvable_path_to_fire names the change -- a recorded kind of 'none' -- and declines to make it in the run's own record; this file makes it in a temporary document a test writes, which is the same change without falsifying anything.
rejection_class.why_a_committed_fixture_rather_than_pros: AAP 0.9.4 requires a committed negative fixture AND an explicit assertion for every rejection condition each exercised adapter can produce, whether or not this run's own artifacts contained the case. This adapter can produce unresolvable_path -- the branch is in the code and the metadata vocabulary mandates it -- so a prose note that the branch exists does not discharge the obligation. A rejection path with no committed fixture is a rejection path nobody has exercised.
rejection_class.branch_precedence_is_why_one_record_was_: The absent_path branch precedes the PATH_BASE_KIND_NONE branch, so a record with an empty filePath would be classified absent_path even under this variant. The sibling fixture's one defective dependency is exactly that shape, which is why it was excluded when this fixture was derived: with it present the fixture would produce two classes, the shared-detail property would be false, and the file could not establish that the class turns on the metadata alone.
rejection_class.the_error_this_prevents: A resolver that treated an unestablished base as 'fall back to the scan root' would emit six rows here that look entirely ordinary -- four tree files and two archive members, all relativized, two of them in scope -- because every path in this artifact happens to be absolute under that very root. Nothing downstream could tell those rows from correctly resolved ones. The fixture exists so the fallback is a rejection rather than a plausible guess.

rejection_boundary.statement: A record whose path cannot be resolved is a rejection. A record that names a location the scope does not cover, or one that is not a plain file in the tree, is a KEPT row with in_scope false. This fixture carries the second kind in quantity -- four of its six records are out-of-glob or archive coordinates -- so the contrast block shows them kept, and the top-level outcome shows that a metadata condition rejects them all regardless of how ordinary their coordinates are.
rejection_boundary.why_it_can_only_be_a_rejection: path is one of only two never-absent fields in the twelve-field schema, the other being severity_norm: emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS carries both, and emit.validate_rows raises on a null in either. A record whose path could not be resolved therefore has nothing to put in the field, and AAP 0.5.4 is explicit that such a record is rejected and counted rather than guessed into a field.

not_a_rejection.expected: the tool's normal convention on this provisioning; relativizing it is the adapter's job
not_a_rejection.evidence: All six records report an absolute path, because the runner passes 18 absolute --scan arguments. Reading absoluteness as a defect would reject every row this tool can ever produce.

not_a_rejection.case: a path outside the twelve authoritative globs
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with in_scope false, counted under rows_out_of_scope
not_a_rejection.evidence: dev/package-lock.json and docs/Gemfile.lock. Both exist in the pinned tree, both are legitimately reachable by a dependency-oriented scanner, and neither matches any glob. AAP 0.9.3 keeps them and AAP 0.8.3 is explicit that an individual out-of-glob coordinate never establishes a wrong scan root.

not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row serialized <container-relative-to-root>!<member>, ! the single separator, in_scope false, counted in non_filesystem_paths
not_a_rejection.evidence: One container inside the root and one outside it whose ../ segments are PRESERVED rather than normalized, per the SARIF 2.1.0 errata amendment to section 3.10.2 that paths.py implements for every shape. Both take in_scope false through ResolvedPath.in_scope, which applies the non-filesystem rule before any glob is tested.

not_a_rejection.case: a path outside the scan root
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row whose ../ segments are preserved and which is never emitted absolute
not_a_rejection.evidence: The local Maven repository container relativizes to ../../root/.m2/repository/... under the recorded base. It is classified archive_member rather than outside_root because the archive test runs first, so path_kind_outside_root is 0 in both blocks -- recorded because a reader tallying that counter would otherwise expect 1.

rejection_boundary.these_three_are_rows_only_under_the_reco: Under this file's variant all four cases above are rejections, and they are rejected for the metadata's reason rather than for anything about their coordinates. That is the point of recording them: an implementation that rejected an out-of-glob or archive coordinate on its own terms would produce the same top-level numbers here for entirely the wrong reason, and the contrast block is what separates the two.
rejection_boundary.no_guessed_path: The six rejected records are rejected and counted, never given a path. Nothing in this file supplies a coordinate for them, and neither their fileName nor their md5/sha1/sha256 is read as one -- the fileName would be ambiguous in any case, since two package-lock.json files exist in the pinned tree, which is why inferring from it is forbidden rather than merely discouraged.
rejection_boundary.the_absolute_values_in_the_identities_ar: Each rejection's identity quotes the filePath the artifact carries, and those are filesystem-absolute. They appear in a rejection record -- the artifact's own value, retained so the record can be found again -- and never in a row's path field. No absolute path is emitted anywhere in the dataset, and the contrast block's six rows are all relative.

counts.raw_count_unit: one element of dependencies[].vulnerabilities[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction, summing len(vulnerabilities) over dependencies[]
counts.raw_count_derivation: sum(len(d.vulnerabilities)) over the seven dependencies = 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 0. The last term is dependency 6, core/src/main/resources/org/apache/spark/ui/static/package.json, which carries no vulnerabilities key at all.
counts.raw_count_authority: harness/lib/normalize/reconcile.py, _count_dependency_check, reached through count_records('dependency-check', doc). It builds no row, resolves no path and reads no metadata, which is the whole point of it: the same six elements count as six under both variants, so the arithmetic below tests the adapter's accounting rather than the document.
counts.rejections_by_class_note: One class, six records, one shared detail. The six are distinguished by their record identities rather than by their details, because the detail names the metadata condition and the metadata condition is the same for all six. All six identities are asserted below.
counts.every_record_yields_exactly_one_outcome: One row or one rejection per record, never both and never neither -- _adapt_vulnerability returns a single value of one of the two types, so the property is structural rather than asserted. Here all six outcomes are rejections, which is the boundary case of the identity worth having a fixture for: rows is 0 and the identity still has to balance.
counts.zero_rows_is_not_an_empty_artifact: The artifact carries six records and the traversal counts six. An adapter that returned nothing at all -- no rows and no rejections -- would satisfy 'zero rows' and fail the identity, which is exactly the failure mode a rejection count exists to catch.

four_reported_counters.authority: AAP 0.5.4 -- the four counts reported per tool
four_reported_counters.note: All four are 0 under this variant, and none of the four zeros means the artifact lacks the shape: multi_valued_cwe_records and non_filesystem_paths are 1 and 2 under the recorded base over the same records. They are 0 here because each is incremented on the row-emitting path only. Named rather than restated with their values -- the counters block is the single measurement, and a number carried twice inside one document is a number that can drift.

counts.parse_status_authority: harness/lib/normalize/cli.py, PARSE_STATUS_PARTIAL = 'partial', assigned as partial where there are rejections and clean where there are none. Partial rather than failed, even with no row emitted: the adapter parsed every record, classified every one and abandoned nothing. A failed parse in this pipeline is an artifact matching no known shape, which halts the run; this artifact matches its shape exactly.
counts.row_order: Not applicable -- there is no row. The rejections are in traversal order, /dependencies/0 through /dependencies/5, and are asserted in that order.
counts.rejection_order_is_traversal_order: The adapter walks dependencies[] once in order and each dependency's vulnerabilities[] once in order, so the rejections come back in traversal order and a test may zip them against the array below positionally. That is asserted rather than assumed: the six identities differ, so a reordering would fail the comparison rather than pass it silently.

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/dependency_check.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): thirty-three keys in that order -- twenty-four authored, plus one path_kind_* per normalize.paths.PATH_KINDS member and one severity_basis_* per normalize.severity.BASIS_VALUES member. Every key is present with a value, including the thirty-one that are 0, because a counter absent from the mapping and a counter at 0 are different claims.
counters_note: Two counters are non-zero and both describe the traversal's shape rather than any record's outcome: dependencies 7 and dependencies_without_vulnerabilities_array 1. Every other counter is 0 because each is incremented on the row-emitting path, after step 4 has passed, and step 4 rejects every record here. That is the sharpest structural claim this file makes: a non-zero severity, cwe, cve, coordinate, path-kind or scope counter would mean a rejected record had been tallied.
counters_arithmetic: dependencies 7 == the seven elements of dependencies[]
dependencies_skipped_non_mapping 0 + dependencies_without_vulnerabilities_array 1 == the one dependency contributing no record; every other dependency is a mapping carrying a vulnerabilities array
rows_in_scope 0 + rows_out_of_scope 0 == rows 0 -- the scope tallies move per emitted row and there is no emitted row, so this is not the claim that nothing was in scope
start_line_absent 0 == rows 0, for the same reason: the counter records an absence on a row rather than the absence of line information in the shape
severity_label_present 0 + severity_label_absent 0 == rows 0, although all six records carry a severity member -- the counter is read during row construction only
every severity_basis_* counter is 0 and they sum to rows 0; under the recorded base they sum to 6 as severity_basis_label 5 + severity_basis_cvss_score 1
every package_coordinate_* counter is 0, including package_coordinate_unformable, although every dependency here carries a formable pkg: URL -- step 5 never runs
every path_kind_* counter is 0 and non_filesystem_paths is 0, so no path of any kind was produced

archive_references_split 0 even though two records' values WERE prepared with the '!' separator before the resolver saw them, which the identities show; the counter is incremented on the row-emitting path, so preparation happening and the counter moving are two different events
multi_valued_cwe_records 0 although record 4 carries two CWE entries, and cwe_absent 0 although two records would have had no CWE -- both counters are row-side
the six counted records are 0 rows + 6 rejections, and no counter above counts a rejected record: a rejection at step 4 never reaches the severity, cwe, cve, coordinate, path-kind or in_scope tallies

prohibitions_observed.no_cross_tool_interpretation: Nothing here compares dependency-check with any other tool. The sibling adapters are named only to say which of them owns a rejection route this fixture does not exercise.
prohibitions_observed.no_judging: No record is called real, important or a false positive. A record that cannot be resolved is a record whose base was not established, which is a statement about the metadata rather than about the finding.
prohibitions_observed.no_dedup: The two records naming the same Guava artifact at two versions, in two different containers, are not merged, and the six records sharing one rejection detail are not merged either: six records produce six rejections. AAP 0.3.2 forbids deduplication in either direction.
prohibitions_observed.no_invented_severity: No severity is chosen here. Under this variant none is reached at all; under the recorded base each row's basis and selected entry are recorded in the contrast block, against a policy fixed before any output was observed.
prohibitions_observed.kept_not_filtered: Nothing is filtered. Under the recorded base all six records become rows, including the two whose paths lie outside the twelve globs and the two archive members, all of which are kept and marked rather than dropped.
prohibitions_observed.rejected_not_dropped: All six records are counted under a named class with a retained detail, so the artifact's six records are six accounted-for outcomes and the identity balances at zero rows.
prohibitions_observed.no_runner_or_metadata_edit: The variant is constructed as a ToolPathBase from a metadata document the calling test writes inside its own temporary directory. harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, harness/bin/run-dependency-check.sh and harness/scope/allowlist.txt are unchanged and must stay so: the first is the gate's record of the provisioning as found, and the other two are provisioned files AAP 0.3.2 forbids editing.
prohibitions_observed.no_secret_or_absolute_emitted_value: No secret, credential or credential-shaped string appears in this file or in the fixture. The absolute values that do appear are the artifact's own filePath strings quoted inside rejection identities, which is the artifact's data retained for locating a record; every path in the contrast block's rows is relative.
prohibitions_observed.never_derived_by_running_the_adapter: Every value in this file -- the detail string, the six record identities and their key order, the thirty-three counters under both variants, the reconciliation arithmetic and the contrast block's six rows -- was derived by reading harness/lib/normalize/adapters/dependency_check.py, harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, harness/lib/normalize/severity.py and this fixture. The detail was read from its literal in resolve_recorded_path's PATH_BASE_KIND_NONE branch, and the identity keys from _adapt_vulnerability's identity dict plus the reported_path setdefault in resolve_recorded_path.
prohibitions_observed.agreement_check_disclosed: After the derivation, the adapter was run over this fixture under both variants once and its output compared with what is written here; it agreed in every field. That check is disclosed as a check and is not the source of these values: had it disagreed, the disagreement would have been diagnosed against the modules rather than pasted in.

corroboration.note: oss-scan-results/findings.json holds 9,433 rows and none of them is a dependency-check row: the tool reported zero findings over the twelve authoritative roots, so there is nothing in the committed dataset to compare against. dependencies_contributing_no_record.reason: The dependency carries no vulnerabilities key at all, so it contributes zero records to the count unit. dependencies_contributing_no_record.in_scope_had_it_produced_a_record: true under the recorded base -- the path matches core/src/main/**. Under this file's variant it would have been rejected like the other six. Either way its absence from the outcomes is a property of the dependency carrying no vulnerability, not of its scope, which is stated so a reader does not read one for the other.
dependencies_contributing_no_record.the_file_itself: 5 lines and 80 bytes at the pin, holding a name, a license and "type": "module", with no dependencies block and no lockfile beside it. It is the only manifest-shaped file inside the twelve authoritative roots, and its emptiness is the reason the dependency-oriented tools resolved nothing in scope.
dependencies_contributing_no_record.path_resolution_never_attempted: Step 4 is never reached for this dependency because no record under it is ever built, so its filePath is neither prepared nor resolved and no counter beyond dependencies_without_vulnerabilities_array moves for it -- under either variant.

contrast_under_the_recorded_base.purpose: The same fixture, adapted with the path base harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json actually records for dependency-check -- kind filesystem_absolute, base value present -- and nothing else changed. It is recorded because the condition this file fixes is a property of the metadata rather than of any record, and a claim of that shape is only checkable against the other branch. It is deliberately a separate block rather than a second set of top-level rows: a loader reading these files generically consumes the top-level rows, counts, rejections and counters, and those describe the variant this file is for.

contrast_under_the_recorded_base.path_basis_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, BASIS_ABSOLUTE_RELATIVIZED -- the basis resolve_recorded_path records where the reported value was filesystem-absolute and was relativized against the root. The basis says what was done rather than implying a resolution that did no work.
contrast_under_the_recorded_base.counters_that_move_only_here: Nineteen counters are non-zero under this base and two under the variant. The seventeen that differ are exactly the row-side counters: the scope pair, start_line_absent, the severity family, the cwe and cve family, the package-coordinate family, the path-kind family, non_filesystem_paths and archive_references_split. The two that agree -- dependencies and dependencies_without_vulnerabilities_array -- are the traversal-shape counters, and their agreement is the check that the traversal itself is unaffected by the metadata.

the_rows.message: Bootstrap contains a cross-site scripting weakness in the carousel component: the data-slide and data-slide-to attributes are written into the document without neutralizing markup, so a page that renders attacker-influenced attribute values can execute script in the browsing context of the page.

The cookie accessor evaluates a stored cookie value as structured data before returning it, so a cookie written by another document on the same registrable domain can influence the object the caller receives.
The glob prefix parser backtracks on a pattern containing many nested braces, so a long crafted pattern costs time superlinear in its length.
Parsing an XML document containing many digits in a numeric character reference takes time superlinear in the length of the reference, so a small document can occupy the parser for a long time.
The temporary directory helper creates a directory readable by every account on the host, so data a caller writes through it is exposed to other local users.
Reading a crafted serialized value through the collection utilities reserves capacity from a size field the input controls, so a short input can exhaust the heap.

the_row_derivations.cvss_disagreement: cvssv3.baseScore 9.1 (baseSeverity CRITICAL) bands Critical and cvssv2.score 4.3 bands Medium, while cvssv4.baseScore 2.3 (baseSeverity LOW) bands Low. The mapped label LOW governs all three, so severity_norm is Low. An implementation reading cvssv3 -- the usual choice -- would emit Critical here, which is why this record is worth carrying.
the_row_derivations.start_line_absent_reason: Dependency-Check reports at dependency granularity and this shape carries no line information at any depth, so start_line is null on every row rather than synthesised.

cwe_source.rule: one entry, so the ascending-numeric rule has nothing to choose between

the_row_derivations.rule_id_source: /dependencies/1/vulnerabilities/0/name -- a RetireJS advisory title rather than a CVE identifier, carried as the rule_id exactly as written
the_row_derivations.case_insensitivity: The literal is lower-case 'moderate'. The label map's keys are upper-case and its lookup upper-cases the observed literal, so MODERATE maps to Medium; severity_native keeps the literal as the tool wrote it, because severity-map.md reports observed literals and folding it here would misreport one the tool never wrote. The record also carries unscored 'true' and no CVSS block, and neither changes the outcome: a mapped label needs no score.
the_row_derivations.cwe_absent_reason: /dependencies/1/vulnerabilities/0/cwes is JSON null, so there is no entry to select from and the field is absent. Counted under cwe_absent.
the_row_derivations.cve_absent_reason: The name is an advisory title, not a CVE-shaped identifier, so no CVE can be taken from it. Counted under cve_absent.

package_coordinate_source.why: The lexicographically smallest candidate at the level wins: 'j' precedes 'n'. Producer order puts the npm entry first and marks it confidence LOW while the javascript entry is HIGH, so neither the array order nor the confidence field decides this -- the stated rule does, and it is the only one of the three that is reproducible. Counted once under package_coordinate_multiple_candidates_at_level.

the_row_derivations.severity_native_source: /dependencies/2/vulnerabilities/0/severity -- a JSON number, not a label
the_row_derivations.float_representation: The artifact carries 5.300000190734863 -- an OSS Index float32 score widened to float64, with the representation tail intact. severity_native carries the one-decimal rendering '5.3', so no artifact tail reaches a text field, and the band is taken from the full-precision number rather than from the rendered text. 5.300000190734863 bands Medium exactly as 5.3 does; rounding cannot cross a boundary at this value.
the_row_derivations.why_the_selected_entry_names_source_labe: The number came from the severity member itself rather than from a versioned CVSS block, so the recorded entry names source 'label' with a null version. That is why this row does NOT increment severity_selected_score_with_source_and_version, which stays 0 for the whole fixture.
the_row_derivations.cve_absent_reason: 'sonatype-2022-6438' is not CVE-shaped, so no CVE can be taken from the name. Counted under cve_absent.
the_row_derivations.out_of_scope_reason: No glob matches dev/package-lock.json. It exists in the pinned tree and is legitimately reachable by a dependency-oriented scanner, so the row is kept with in_scope false rather than dropped, and an out-of-glob coordinate never establishes a wrong scan root.

the_row_derivations.cvss_agreement: cvssv3.baseScore 6.5, baseSeverity MEDIUM -- bands Medium, agreeing with the label that governed. Recorded so the label-over-score rule is visible as a rule rather than only where the two disagree.

cwe_source.rule: The one entry carries no CWE-\d+ identifier, so nothing can be selected from it. The entry is counted under cwe_entries_without_identifier and the field is absent, counted under cwe_absent -- an entry that exists but names no identifier is distinguished from no entry at all, which is the distinction the two counters exist for.

the_row_derivations.cwe_absent_reason: The only entry is the NVD placeholder 'NVD-CWE-noinfo', which names no identifier.
the_row_derivations.out_of_scope_reason: No glob matches docs/Gemfile.lock. Kept with in_scope false, as row 2.

the_row_derivations.cvss_agreement: cvssv3.baseScore 7.1, baseSeverity HIGH -- bands High, agreeing with the label that governed.
the_row_derivations.reported_path_form: filesystem-absolute AND concatenated: the container path with the member joined onto it by a '/' and no separator, exactly the shape dependency_check.prepare_file_path exists for
the_row_derivations.path_note: prepare_file_path inserts the single '!' at the first segment whose extension names a container -- the '.jar' element -- and paths.py then relativizes the container and serializes <container>!<member>. Without the split the coordinate would relativize into an ordinary-looking path naming a file that is not on disk. Counted once under archive_references_split.

cwe_source.rule: ascending numeric identifier: 379 < 552. Producer order lists CWE-552 first, so an implementation taking the first entry would emit the other value -- which is why the ordering is stated rather than left to the array. Counted once under multi_valued_cwe_records.

the_row_derivations.out_of_scope_reason: An archive member is never in scope: paths.in_scope applies the non-filesystem rule before any glob is tested. Independently, the container's own segments match no glob either -- it sits under common/network-common/target/, not common/network-common/src/main/ -- so both reasons agree here. They are recorded separately because the kind rule is the one that decides.

the_row_derivations.cvss_agreement: cvssv3.baseScore 5.9, baseSeverity MEDIUM -- bands Medium, agreeing with the label that governed.
the_row_derivations.reported_path_form: filesystem-absolute, outside the scan root, AND concatenated -- the local Maven repository copy of the same Guava POM
the_row_derivations.path_note: The container sits outside the root, so relativizing it yields ../ segments, and those segments are PRESERVED rather than normalized -- the SARIF 2.1.0 errata amendment to section 3.10.2, which paths.py implements for every shape. The serialized coordinate is therefore ../../root/.m2/.../guava-18.0.jar!META-INF/... and no absolute value is emitted. Counted under archive_references_split and non_filesystem_paths.
the_row_derivations.why_not_outside_root: paths.path_kind_for tests for the archive separator BEFORE it tests whether the path escapes the root, so a member inside a container outside the root is archive_member rather than outside_root. Both kinds are non-filesystem coordinates and both take in_scope false, so the discriminator changes which counter moves and nothing else. Recorded because a reader tallying path_kind_outside_root would otherwise expect 1.
the_row_derivations.out_of_scope_reason: An archive member is never in scope, and this container is outside the root as well. As row 4, the kind rule is the one that decides.

contrast_under_the_recorded_base.what_the_contrast_establishes: Six records, unchanged, with opposite outcomes under two path bases and no other difference. Every path in this artifact is absolute under the very root a fall-back resolver would have defaulted to, so a resolver that treated an unestablished base as 'use the scan root' would emit these six rows under the variant too, and nothing in the dataset could distinguish them. The two blocks together are what make that failure detectable: the same input, one input changed, two outcomes that must not be the same.
contrast_under_the_recorded_base.why_the_rows_are_recorded_in_full: So the contrast is checkable rather than asserted. A block claiming 'six rows here, none there' with no rows in it would be a summary of a run; these six rows are derived from the fixture field by field, and each one's derivation is recorded beside it at the same depth the sibling positive and negative expectations use.

package_coordinate_precedence.authority: AAP 0.5.4's one candidate precedence for every dependency-oriented shape, implemented by harness/lib/normalize/adapters/dependency_check.py's package_coordinate(). The four levels are exercised across this tree; oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/expected/dependency-check.rows.json is the reference case for the precedence as a whole.
package_coordinate_precedence.reached_under_this_variant: Nothing. Step 5 runs after step 4 and step 4 rejects every record, so no level is consulted and every package_coordinate_* counter is 0 -- including package_coordinate_unformable, which is 0 because the question was never asked rather than because every coordinate was formable.

package_object_package_url.rule: a package URL on the enclosing package object -- for this shape the enclosing dependency's packages[] entries, pooled across every entry before the tiebreak is applied
package_object_package_url.note: Every row resolves at level 2, because every dependency here carries a packages[] entry whose id is a pkg: URL. Level 1 is unreached (no record carries its own purl/packageUrl/packageURL/package_url member), and levels 3 and 4 are unreached because level 2 stops first.

package_coordinate_precedence.tiebreak: Where several candidates sit at one level the lexicographically smallest wins, over the pooled candidates of the whole level rather than within one package object -- taking the first entry's value instead would make the coordinate depend on producer order.

tiebreak_exercised_by.why: 'pkg:javascript/...' sorts before 'pkg:npm/...' because 'j' precedes 'n'. Producer order puts the npm entry first and marks it confidence LOW while the javascript entry is HIGH, so neither the array order nor the confidence field decides this: the stated lexicographic rule does, and it is the only one of the three that is reproducible.
tiebreak_exercised_by.counter: package_coordinate_multiple_candidates_at_level, 1 under the recorded base and 0 under the variant

package_coordinate_precedence.every_rejected_record_had_one: All six rejected records sit under a dependency carrying a formable pkg: URL, so a coordinate was available for each and none of them reached it. That ordering is why package_coordinate_from_package_object_package_url is 0 under the variant and 6 under the recorded base, and it is asserted rather than incidental: a coordinate counter that moved for a rejected record would mean the classification order had been reordered.
package_coordinate_precedence.unformable_belongs_elsewhere: Where no candidate can be formed at any level the field is not emitted null: for this dependency-oriented shape the record is rejected under unformable_package_coordinate. That case belongs to oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/reject-dependency-check-no-package-coordinate.json.

severity_policy.authority: harness/lib/normalize/severity.py -- the case-insensitive label map, the CVSS v3.1 section 5 band table, and resolve()'s ordered precedence. Nothing is mapped or banded in the adapter.
severity_policy.reached_under_this_variant: Nothing. Severity is resolved on the row-emitting path only, so no record here reaches severity.resolve and none is fed to the LiteralTally. This fixture under this variant contributes nothing at all to oss-scan-results/severity-map.md -- and that is the assertion, not an omission: six tally entries here would report six literals against zero rows.
severity_policy.label_over_score: A native label in the mapped vocabulary governs whatever the scores say; a score is consulted only where no mapped label exists. Either way the entry used is recorded -- the label, or the score with its source and version. Five of the six records carry a mapped label and one carries a bare number, which is why the recorded base yields severity_basis_label 5 and severity_basis_cvss_score 1.
severity_policy.bands: 9.0-10.0 Critical, 7.0-8.9 High, 4.0-6.9 Medium, 0.1-3.9 Low, 0.0 Info. The boundaries and the first four labels are the CVSS v3.1 section 5 standard's; the standard's None band is emitted under this dataset's own label Info, which is a mapping this dataset defines and not a CVSS label. Banding is by ordered numeric comparison, never lexical.
severity_policy.severity_native_rendering: A label reaches severity_native as the literal the tool wrote, stripped of surrounding whitespace and neither case-folded nor coerced -- which is why the contrast block's row 1 carries lower-case 'moderate'. A numeric severity reaches it as a one-decimal rendering of the full-precision value, which is why row 2 carries '5.3' and not the float32 tail.

label_versus_score_disagreements.label: LOW
label_versus_score_disagreements.note: A wide disagreement on one record: three CVSS blocks spanning Critical, Medium and Low beside a LOW label. An implementation reading cvssv3 -- the usual choice -- emits Critical. What the label-over-score rule changes here is which entry is recorded as having governed, and that is the checkable difference. Under this file's own variant the record is rejected before any of it is read.

float_representation_artifact.origin: An OSS Index-sourced record carries no label and Dependency-Check renders the provider's float CVSS score into the severity field, so the float32-to-float64 representation tail reaches the artifact verbatim. The value is in the fixture exactly as written here.
float_representation_artifact.path_taken: The severity member is a JSON number rather than a mapped label, and the record carries no CVSS block at all, so the number is banded as a score in its own right. The recorded entry names source 'label' with a null version -- the value came from the severity member, not from a versioned CVSS block -- which is why this row does NOT increment severity_selected_score_with_source_and_version, and why that counter is 0 in both blocks.
float_representation_artifact.banding: Numeric, on the full-precision value rather than on the rendered text: 5.300000190734863 bands Medium exactly as 5.3 does. Rounding to one decimal place cannot cross a band boundary at this value, and the band is never taken from the rendered text.
float_representation_artifact.no_spurious_precision: severity_native carries the one-decimal rendering, so no artifact tail reaches a text field. The full-precision value appears in this file only as a JSON number under selected_entry.score, which is where severity.py keeps it.

case_insensitivity.note: Absorbed by the case-insensitive map, whose keys are upper-case and whose lookup upper-cases the observed literal. The literal is preserved as written rather than folded, because severity-map.md reports observed literals with per-literal row counts and upper-casing it here would misreport a literal the tool never wrote. The record also carries unscored 'true' and no CVSS block, and neither changes the outcome: a mapped label needs no score.

severity_policy.never_absent: severity_norm is absent on no row in either block. severity_native is absent on no row either -- every record carries a severity member -- so severity_basis_no_vocabulary is 0 under both variants.
severity_policy.unmapped_literals: None. Every literal on an emitted row is either a mapped label or a bandable number in 0.0-10.0, so severity_basis_unmapped_literal is 0 under both variants.

in_scope_surface.statement: This tool's only in-scope surface at the pin is the vendored web bundles under core/src/main/resources: 30 .js and 10 .css, 40 files, counted on the pinned tree at 59b8a4489c878fa3a9aa6b7fbae760f2fc80eb9d. Two of this fixture's records name two of them, and under the recorded base they are the only two in_scope true rows.
in_scope_surface.under_this_variant: Zero rows, so zero in-scope rows and zero out-of-scope rows. rows_in_scope 0 does not mean nothing was in scope -- two of the six coordinates are -- it means no row was emitted for the allowlist to be consulted about.

in_scope_surface.what_this_provisioning_actually_resolved: harness/artifacts/raw/dependency-check.json carries 32 dependencies -- 31 .js files and that one package.json -- with zero vulnerabilities and zero packages among them. No .css file became a dependency at all. The 40-file figure above is the in-scope bundle surface on disk; the 32 is what the tool resolved from it. Two different measurements, both stated, neither substituted for the other.
in_scope_surface.no_scope_judgement: Recorded as a property of the scope, exactly as AAP 0.3.2 requires: the allowlist is not widened to give this tool something to resolve, and zero manifests in scope is a fact to report rather than a condition to fix.
